## 1. Configure and read saved state
Manual and staggered hourly runs use the same private source and destination. Check configuration, create the Data Table when needed, and read saved requests before choosing new work. One record is processed per execution.

parameters.content:
## 2. Join and qualify a useful brief
Only confirmed arrivals within the notice window qualify; source and instruction rows must be marked public-only and explicit access-code fields are rejected.

## 3. Recover durable state
Use frozen inputs and accepted jobs from the Data Table. Resume pending work even after its notice window expires. Changed content needs a new revision. Ambiguous paid responses stop for reconciliation. Saved media retries delivery; saved job IDs resume polling.

## 4. Validate and preview a draft
Free validation supplies the quote and enforces the credit cap. dryRun=true attempts a fresh editor draft or inspects saved state, without submitting paid work, uploading files or marking delivery.

## 5. Submit and checkpoint
Save intent before the nonretrying paid request, then persist the accepted job immediately. A lost acceptance response requires reconciliation. Polling retries reuse the saved job instead of paying for another render.

## 6. Retain completed media
Poll within the configured budget. A timeout or missing upload retains the job for investigation. Only completed HTTPS media enters delivery, and its URL is saved before any file operation.

## 7. Deliver a private asset
Search by deterministic filename and folder before uploading. Reuse an MP4 only when its saved content hash matches. Downloads are ordinary media GETs; supported Zvid operations use native nodes. Failed uploads are reconciled on the next run.

## 8. Protect the business source
Persist the Drive ID and reread both registers. Compare their content fingerprint with the frozen request before writeback. Deleted, revised or edited sources stop with the uploaded asset retained.

## 9. Verify the handoff receipt
Write delivery columns, then reread the source and related rows. Only a matching revision, content fingerprint, job and file receipt marks the ledger delivered. Failed verification retains the upload for retry.

## 10. Review the recorded outcome
The ledger and source register retain the result and private Drive link. Review Watch video → Binary → data → View. Preview retries are bounded; a failed preview leaves the completed delivery intact.

## Accommodation details to a public arrival guide video

### How it works
Prepare a private guest arrival briefing using approved public guidance, excluding access credentials. A private Drive MP4, with full source records retained in Sheets and the n8n ledger, plus asset links, revision, job ID and handoff summary written back to D52Source for accommodation operators. The workflow reads a source register and related rows, applies its approval and eligibility rules, and creates a concise review video. Fingerprints suppress completed revisions; a Data Table retains accepted jobs and delivery checkpoints. Retries resume polling or delivery. An ambiguous paid response requires reconciliation. Each execution handles one record.

### Setup
1. Install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`** from **Settings → Community nodes** before Zvid credentials; a workspace owner/admin may need to install it.
2. Create **Zvid API** credentials at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys, Base URL `https://api.zvid.io`; select them on all Zvid nodes. Connect **Google Sheets** and **Google Drive OAuth2**.
3. In **Config**, set spreadsheetId, sourceSheet, detailsSheet and driveFolderId. Create the domain columns and delivery headers from the included `hotel-arrival-guide-video.md` guide. Keep source_id unique and increment revision for changed content.
4. **`dryRun: false` renders and spends credits** within maxRenderCredits. True returns an editor draft attempt and quote.
5. Run manually once, inspect the Drive asset and register update, then enable the hourly trigger. Avoid parallel manual runs. **Watch video → Binary → data → View** previews completed media.

[Zvid setup reference](https://docs.zvid.io). Support: https://zvid.io/contact
